title: Air Pollution Is Slowing Down Marathon Runners — Study
paragraphs: Running a marathon is hard enough. But according to a new study from the UK, dirty air may make it even harder, especially for ordinary runners.

The study was carried out by researchers at the University of Leicester and supported by the British Heart Foundation. The researchers looked at the finishing times of more than 2.7 million runners in six of the world's biggest marathons: Berlin, Boston, Chicago, London, New York City and Tokyo. The races took place between 2010 and 2024.

The researchers compared the runners' times with the levels of air pollution on the day of each race. They found that higher levels of nitrogen dioxide were linked to slower times for both men and women. This gas mainly comes from burning fossil fuels, for example in cars and factories. However, another type of pollution, tiny particles in the air, was not clearly linked to slower times.

The effect was much bigger for ordinary runners than for top athletes. For every small increase in nitrogen dioxide, recreational runners finished 2.12 minutes slower. Elite runners finished only 0.34 minutes slower. On a day with high pollution, finishing times were about seven to eight minutes longer than on a day with low pollution.

Among the six cities, London had the highest levels of nitrogen dioxide on race day, while Berlin had the lowest. However, pollution levels on the day of the London Marathon have fallen a lot since 2010.

Why were ordinary runners affected more? The researchers suggest that one reason is that slower runners spend more time on the course, so they breathe in more polluted air. Also, top runners often train in places with cleaner air.
The study does not prove that pollution causes slower times. However, the researchers say that people should not stop running. Exercise is still very good for the heart.
